title: Acids and Bases
seo_title: Grade 10 Science: Acids and Bases Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Acids and bases: properties of acids and bases, the pH scale and indicators, neutralization, and acids and bases in the environment and everyday life. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 10, Chemistry)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 science worksheets (BC): properties of acids and bases, the pH scale, indicators, neutralization and salts, and acid rain. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: pH below 7 is acidic; above 7 is basic.
body_html:
How to think about it

Acids taste sour, turn blue litmus red and react with metals; bases feel slippery and turn red litmus blue. The pH scale runs from 0 to 14: pH 7 is neutral, lower is acidic and higher is basic. Each step is 10 times stronger.

In neutralization, an acid and a base react to make a salt and water: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O. Acid rain forms when sulfur and nitrogen oxides from burning fuel dissolve in rain.

Example

Lemon juice has pH 2. Is it acidic or basic?

Below 7

Answer: acidic

Example

What are the products of HCl + KOH?

Acid + base → salt + water

Answer: KCl and water

Common mistakes

  • Thinking pH 4 is twice as acidic as pH 8 (it is 10 000 times).
  • Thinking all salts are table salt.
  • Thinking bases are always safe (some burn skin).

add dilute acid (effervescence; the gas (carbon dioxide) turns limewater milky)
items.e: sulfate, SO₄²⁻: acidify with dilute nitric acid, then add aqueous barium nitrate.
